item.title: We tried to automate Epoch
item.description: Epoch tested leading AI models on its own regular work tasks, graded against the standards applied to human employees, and found the best scored about sixty-five percent, which is still a failing grade. This helps explain why AI's economic impact lags behind its benchmark results. Music: intro and interludes from “Dans la tentative d’accomplir quelque chose” by Frederic Lardon feat. Laura Palmée (CC0). Outro: “Crap Transition” by Jesse Spillane, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/Jesse_Spillane/Art_of_Presentation/Jesse_Spillane_-_Art_of_Presentation_-_04_Crap_Transition/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

item.title: Andy Burnham defends Gogglebox appearance after Badenoch criticism
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham defended appearing on a celebrity Gogglebox episode for Stand Up To Cancer after Kemi Badenoch said she was amazed he had the time. Badenoch argued that a prime minister should be focused on the job rather than Gogglebox and social media. Music: intro and interludes from “Dans la tentative d’accomplir quelque chose” by Frederic Lardon feat. Laura Palmée (CC0). item.title: Your Book Review: We Present Television
item.description: A reviewer reads a 1940 collection of essays by the pioneers of American television, and finds it mostly prosaic technical description laced with startlingly accurate, and sometimes eerie, prophecy about the world television would build. The reviewer argues that "Television" meant far more than the TV set, and that its authors foresaw much of our connected, screen-saturated present. Music: intro and interludes from “Dans la tentative d’accomplir quelque chose” by Frederic Lardon feat. Laura Palmée (CC0). Outro: “Crap Transition” by Jesse Spillane, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/Jesse_Spillane/Art_of_Presentation/Jesse_Spillane_-_Art_of_Presentation_-_04_Crap_Transition/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

item.title: Your Book Review: Storm Of Steel
item.description: The reviewer argues that Ernst Jünger's Storm of Steel is the best war novel ever written, because it reports the First World War without a thesis. He links its theme of death and duty to his own ordeal when his daughter was born at twenty-four weeks. Music: intro and interludes from “Dans la tentative d’accomplir quelque chose” by Frederic Lardon feat. Laura Palmée (CC0). item.title: Our AI Midwife
item.description: A father describes how a chatbot playing a TV doctor suggested the MRI that found a fibroid behind his wife's six years of unexplained infertility, leading to a natural pregnancy after surgery. He uses the story to argue that AI's everyday benefits deserve acknowledgment alongside its risks. Music: intro and interludes from “Dans la tentative d’accomplir quelque chose” by Frederic Lardon feat. Laura Palmée (CC0). Outro: “Crap Transition” by Jesse Spillane, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/Jesse_Spillane/Art_of_Presentation/Jesse_Spillane_-_Art_of_Presentation_-_04_Crap_Transition/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

item.title: Can AI automate AI R&D yet?
item.description: Using an evaluation called InnovationEval, the piece tests whether frontier AI models can independently rediscover a recent machine learning innovation, and finds they fall far short, reaching at most fifteen percent of the original gains while overstating their results. Progress is fast, so the authors plan to repeat the test on newer models. Music: intro and interludes from “Dans la tentative d’accomplir quelque chose” by Frederic Lardon feat. Laura Palmée (CC0). Outro: “Crap Transition” by Jesse Spillane, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/Jesse_Spillane/Art_of_Presentation/Jesse_Spillane_-_Art_of_Presentation_-_04_Crap_Transition/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.

item.title: Current AIs out-persuade professionals in lab settings but (probably) not in the world
item.description: The author argues that experiments show AIs beating professional humans at narrow persuasion tasks, but real-world evidence suggests broad AI persuasion sits between median human and median professional level. Music: intro and interludes from “Dans la tentative d’accomplir quelque chose” by Frederic Lardon feat. Laura Palmée (CC0). item.title: The Bitter Lesson
item.description: Looking back over decades of AI research, the piece argues that general methods which scale with computation, namely search and learning, have always eventually beaten approaches that build in human knowledge, and that researchers should build meta-methods that discover rather than encode what we think we know. Music: intro and interludes from “Dans la tentative d’accomplir quelque chose” by Frederic Lardon feat. Laura Palmée (CC0). Outro: “Crap Transition” by Jesse Spillane, https://freemusicarchive.org/music/Jesse_Spillane/Art_of_Presentation/Jesse_Spillane_-_Art_of_Presentation_-_04_Crap_Transition/ licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); trimmed, faded and mixed with narration.
